title: Install beads_watch under systemd --user with linger
description: Unit is at systemd/beads_watch.service. Install: cp systemd/beads_watch.service ~/.config/systemd/user/ && systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user enable --now beads_watch && loginctl enable-linger goku. Without linger the daemon dies on logout and the tailnet endpoint 502s.
close_reason: Enabled via systemctl --user enable --now ~/dev/beads_watch/systemd/beads_watch.service (unit symlinked from the repo rather than copied, so repo edits + daemon-reload apply). Daemon active on /run/user/1000/beads_watch.sock, serving 13 repos. Linger was already enabled (loginctl show-user: Linger=yes). Done while wiring up the a44.beads Omarchy shell widget.

title: One bad repo path in config crash-loops the whole daemon
description: Startup validation stats every configured repo path and exits on the first failure, so a single stale entry (deleted repo, path invisible to the unit — PrivateTmp hides /tmp, for example) takes every other repo down with it, and systemd auto-restart loops forever. Discovered while wiring omabeads' add-repo cog: a path that existed for the caller but not inside the service namespace killed 14 repos. omabeads defends itself with backup/health-poll/rollback, but the daemon could instead serve the repos it can stat and report the bad one as ok:false with an error — the shape GET /v1/repos already has.

title: Switch tailscale serve from localhost TCP to the unix socket
description:
Currently served as: tailscale serve --bg --https=443 http://127.0.0.1:7717. The unix socket is preferred (mode 0600 shuts out other local users; localhost TCP does not). Serving a unix socket requires root, so this needs one operator command:

  sudo tailscale serve --https=443 off
  sudo tailscale serve --bg --https=443 unix:/run/user/1000/beads_watch.sock

Then restart the daemon without --listen so it binds the socket from config.
